scenario: Young couple saving for a first home deposit, considering an ISA wrapper.
transcript: I'm 28, my partner is 30, we live in Manchester and rent for £1,150 a month. Combined take-home is about £4,800. We've got £14,000 in a Monzo savings pot that we've been adding to for two years. We're thinking we want to buy somewhere in maybe three years. We've heard about ISAs but I honestly don't really know the difference between them. Should we be doing something smarter with this money?
expected_llm_claims: Stocks & Shares ISAs allow tax-free growth on investments up to £20,000 per tax year.
You should open a Lifetime ISA with Hargreaves Lansdown and put £4,000 in immediately.
Investing for three years carries more capital risk than holding cash.
This strategy is risk-free for first-time buyers.
